title: Signal / noise sheet
summary: Your round-1 pick (C) kept as a calm paper sheet, now in the blended language: the principle in sentence case with one light accent, nine lines of market noise that settle into the single line entering 'the clearest', and one clean line leaving it for the red tick on the frame edge.

reference.site: Round 1 · C 'Signal / noise sheet' (Heron AI), with A's head grammar
reference.borrowed: From C (after Heron's 'We're architects…' sheet): an almost empty framed sheet with registration marks, the principle set large between a noisy input on the left and one clean output line on the right, a datum running through the statement at the line 'the clearest', lettered A / B marginalia flush to the frame edges, and a single red tick where the output lands on the frame. From A: the head grammar, meaning the red-square caps label, the two-voice statement in sentence case, the 48×2 red rule and the 20px support line.
reference.kelwin: Everything C wrapped around the drawing is gone: the cell walls, the crosshairs at the walls, the 48px bottom band with its legend, the SHEET 07/14 · REV C title cells and the logo mark. What remains is a registration frame (four corner marks only) and a text column that starts on col 4 so cols 1–3 can hold the input. There is no title block: the figure number rides the label row ('Fig. 07' at the right), exactly as on every other section, so the sheet ends on the support line alone. C's 22 tiny vertical ticks become DIRECTION-AC's CONTOUR primitive: nine open 1px curves at a fixed 12px spacing, spiky where they enter the sheet and calmer as they approach the statement, closing onto the datum so that only the middle line (in --fg) carries on into 'the clearest'. The output wire is set in the same line box as 'the clearest', so it starts 32px after the word and runs to the frame edge in both skins. C's 11px mono marginalia become kit callout tags: a 12px mono code box with a 14px Mona label ('A · Input · market noise', 'B · Output · one signal'), each seated 17px under the drawing it names (A under the noise bundle, B under the red tick). The caps title becomes 'In a noisy market, / the clearest / company wins.' at the kit's 112px manifesto size, with 'the clearest company wins.' as the single light accent.

motion: entrance (kit head choreography): the four registration marks fade in at the frame corners (120–360ms). The label row fades in, the three statement lines rise from their masks (80 / 280 / 400ms), the red rule draws and the support line fades up 12px.

orchestrated moment, CONTOUR 'noise settles into signal': the raw bundle plots left → right from the frame edge while the statement rises (clip wipe, 1000ms from 300ms) and the A · Input tag fades in under it. Nine spiky lines, loud and full-spread, end ragged short of the statement. From 1.3s a filter front travels left → right for 1.8s (JS sample interpolation, --ease-inout): amplitude falls, frequency settles, the spread closes onto the datum and the outer lines retract to where they meet it, until one line enters 'the clearest'.

resolution: the output wire draws from 32px after 'the clearest' to the frame edge (scaleX, 800ms from 2.75s). The red tick seats on the frame edge (opacity plus an 8px settle, 420ms from 3.45s), then the B · Output tag fades in beneath it (3.6s). Everything has landed by about 4.0s, and the motion has travelled the reading path: noise → the statement → the one signal out.
ambient: none. It is a pause between two dense graphite sections, so once the noise has settled the sheet holds still.
interaction: none. There are no controls.

on the live site: the sequence plays once when the sheet is 40% visible (IntersectionObserver, no pin, no scrub). Reduced motion renders the filtered drawing synchronously, with the wire and tick in place and no timers. With no script at all, the HTML already holds the filtered paths.
notes: The stage is 813px: 160px of padding at the top and bottom, with the registration frame 64px outside the content box, so the marks sit 96px from each cut. The datum is the x-height centre of line 2. It is 185px below the statement's top, and the noise field is placed on that line. The wire's offset is set in em, calc(50% + .115em), so it stays on the same datum in the Kelwin skin, where Instrument Sans is narrower and the wire simply starts earlier (x 992 instead of 1025). Red appears only on the label square, the 48×2 rule and the output tick, which is the section's one red moment (DIRECTION-AC §5.2). The noise is a seeded drawing (mulberry32), not data, so it carries no Specimen label. Section numbering follows round 2: statechange is FIG. 06 and method is FIG. 08, so this sheet is FIG. 07. The title block was removed in review: its neighbours (architecture, statechange, method) all close on a boxed FIG. title block, so dropping it here keeps the principle a distinct, quieter beat. · Promoted unchanged from round-2 slot X.
addressed: Approved in round 2 — kept as is.
Moved to straight after the system: it now reads as what the closed loop produces — one clear signal out of the noise.
story: The release after the pinned system: what the closed loop produces — one clear signal out of the noise. “Not the loudest. Not the busiest.” answers the letter's “more activity”.
